27343:
• The bill amends the rules surrounding collective agreement decrees and regulates several aspects of the construction industry, particularly with respect to health and safety.
  • It also reduces certain administrative obligations imposed on joint committees and the minister.
Part 1 Act respecting collective agreement decrees
  • The Minister of Labour now decides on amendments to a decree following a request from a joint committee or a contracting party.
  • The Minister may approve, amend or repeal the regulations of joint committees.
  • A uniform non-renewal process is created, requiring notice to the Minister during the sixth month before the decree's expiry.
  • The Minister must verify the representativeness of employer and union associations before recommending a decree or amending one.
  • The Minister may establish directives on the sound governance of joint committees, particularly regarding inspection.
  • The obligation to publish a notice in newspapers when applying for an extension or amendment is eliminated.
  • Joint committees no longer have to submit their budget forecasts and audited financial statements to the Minister annually.
  • Joint committees no longer need to be recognized as training mutuals to participate in workforce skills development.
Part 2 Act respecting Labour Standards
  • The government will be able to establish, by regulation, sectoral labour standards for trades, industries or occupations whose decree has expired.
Part 3 Act respecting Labour Relations, Vocational Training and Workforce Management in the Construction Industry
  • Clarifications are made regarding the working conditions of health and safety representatives on construction sites.
Part 4 Act respecting Labour Relations... construction
  • Rules specify the deployment or withdrawal of health and safety representatives and coordinators according to the start-up and completion phases of the work.
  • The total cost of the work is no longer a criterion for designating these representatives or coordinators.
  • The project owner must notify representative associations when a full-time health and safety representative must be designated.
  • Work performed by permanent employees of the Société des établissements de plein air du Québec, housing cooperatives and non-profit housing organizations is excluded from the Act.
  • The government will be able to implement pilot projects to study or improve the standards applicable to the construction industry.
  • The Commission de la construction du Québec will be able to create a supplementary preventive withdrawal program for pregnant or breastfeeding workers, in addition to the existing program.
  • The administration of this supplementary program will be entrusted to the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail, under an agreement between the two commissions.
  • The Commission de la construction du Québec will be able to grant temporary work authorizations conferring the same rights as a competency certificate, according to criteria it determines.
Part 5 Act respecting Occupational Health and Safety
  • Clarifications are added regarding the working conditions and benefits of health and safety representatives on construction sites.
Part 6 Act respecting Industrial Accidents and Occupational Diseases, Sectoral Decrees and the Regulation respecting prevention mechanisms
  • Housekeeping amendments are made to align with the other changes in the bill.

• The bill creates a new right allowing a person who is worried to obtain information about an intimate partner who may pose a risk to their safety.
  • It establishes a comprehensive process involving the Sûreté du Québec and a designated body to handle these requests and disclose the information.
  • New act respecting the disclosure of information: a person at risk, or someone acting on their behalf with their consent, may request information about their intimate partner.
  • New act: a minor aged 14 or over may submit such a request on their own.
  • New act: the government may, by regulation, designate other persons or categories of persons who may submit a request.
  • New act: police officers and workers from support organizations may inform a person at risk about the request process if it could benefit them.
  • New act: a police officer may, in these cases, disclose the identity of the partner who is the subject of a possible request.
  • New act: the Sûreté du Québec conducts the searches and transmits the relevant information to a body designated by the minister responsible for the status of women.
  • New act: a designated person, subject to regulatory conditions, meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information or the absence of relevant information.
  • New act: this person may also direct the person at risk to specialized resources and provide additional information.
  • New act: restrictions govern the disclosure to the intimate partner of the existence of a request and personal information concerning them.
  • New act: rules limit the further communication and use of the information obtained.
  • New act: certain persons benefit from immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their duties related to this process.
  • New act: these persons cannot be compelled to testify before a court concerning this information.
  • New act: penal offences are provided for breaches of the rules on communication or use of information.
  • Act respecting the Québec correctional system: revises the rules on disclosing to victims information concerning incarcerated persons or those under the supervision of correctional services.
  • Act respecting the Ministère de la Sécurité publique: consequential adjustments related to the creation of the new information disclosure regime.
